S1:31.text: And immediatly the ſunne roſe to him, after that he was paſt Phanuel; but he halted halted on his foote.

S1:32.text: For which cauſe the children of Iſrael eate not the ſinowe, that ſhrunke in Iacobes thighe, vnto his preſent day becauſe he touched the ſinowe of his thighe, and it ſhrunke.

S1:5.text: I haue oxen, and aſſes, and ſheepe, and men ſeruants, and wemen ſeruants: and now I ſend a leagacie to my lord, that I may finde grace in thy ſight

S1:6.text: And the meſſengers returned to Iacob, ſaying We came to Eſau thy brother, and behold he cometh with ſpede to mete thee with foure hundred men.

S1:7.text: Jacob feared exceedingly: & being ſore affraid diuided the people that was with him, the hockes alſo and the ſhepe and the oxen, and the camels, into two troupes.

S1:9.text: And Iacob ſaid: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Iſaac O Lord that dideſt ſay to me Returne into thy land, and into the place of thy nativitie, and I wil doe thee good.

S3:12.text: Thou dideſt ſay that thou wouldeſt do good to me, and dilate my ſeed as the ſand of the ſea, which for multitude can not be numbred.
